d.title: What FastMCP hides, and the three cases where you need it back
d.caption: **Almost every server should be a dozen lines of `@mcp.tool()`**, because the decorator generates the schemas, handles the handshake and picks the transport from one argument. **The three rows in the middle are what the convenience layer is deciding for you** — the name and version a client sees, which transport is served, and whether the server may push notifications at all. A server that has not declared `tools_changed` during initialisation cannot usefully send the notification later.

d.title: stdio is protected by being a subprocess; HTTP is not protected by anything
d.caption: **A stdio server is reachable only by the process that spawned it, and that is the entire access control.** Move the same code to an SSE or streamable-HTTP endpoint and every tool on it — including the destructive ones, backed by the server's own credentials — is available to whoever can send a POST. **It is an ASGI application, so it inherits every concern from lesson 12.1**, authentication in front of it most of all, plus the buffering problem from 10.2: an SSE stream behind a buffering proxy is not a stream.
